Deficit refers to the difference between income and the amount spent in a given period. Debt refers to the principal and interest which will have to be repaid at some point in the future. Debt is not income, so incurring debt to make payments when in deficit doesn't cure the deficit, just how to pay for spending. I think this is the connection you are drawing.

However, debt can increase even without borrowing for deficit spending if interest on existing debt is compounded rather than paid. It is not only a matter of new borrowing for the purpose of new spending. That would be included in calculating deficits. Compounded interest, on the other hand, is just part of existing long term debt and is not included in calculating deficits or surpluses. So you could run a surplus and still have debt increase if you are not paying down the principal on your debt and/or making interest payments for all interest accrued during the period in question.
